security_audit.summary: The static alerts are false positives caused by documentation examples and Markdown code fences in SKILL.md. SQLModel Session.exec calls are ORM query execution, not Python code execution or process execution. No evidence of prompt injection, data exfiltration, malicious execution, or packaged sensitive data was found.

remediation.issue: Documentation examples can trigger scanners because SQLModel uses a method named exec.
remediation.suggestion: Add a short note that db.exec is SQLModel session execution, not Python exec or shell execution.

remediation.issue: The production database example includes a placeholder fallback URL with user and pass text.
remediation.suggestion: Require DATABASE_URL in production examples or use a clearly invalid placeholder without credential-like values.

content.value_statement: Teams often need consistent database patterns for async services, models, migrations, and performance work. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code reusable SQLModel and SQLAlchemy guidance.
actual_capabilities: Explains async SQLAlchemy and SQLModel connection patterns with session cleanup.
Shows model structures for users, tasks, tags, relationships, indexes, and soft deletion.
Describes repository methods for create, read, update, delete, count, and filtered lists.
Provides migration guidance for initial tables, constraints, and indexes.
Covers performance checks, slow query analysis, table statistics, and production checklist items.
limitations: Examples are Python-focused and do not cover every database driver.
The skill provides patterns and guidance; it does not connect to a live database by itself.
Production settings must be reviewed against the target cloud provider and compliance needs.
Some snippets may need updates for specific SQLAlchemy, SQLModel, or Pydantic versions.

use_cases.title: Create an async service database layer
use_cases.description: Plan sessions, models, repositories, and tests for a Python web service.

use_cases.title: Prepare production database settings
use_cases.description: Review pooling, SSL, backups, monitoring, and slow query thresholds before launch.

use_cases.title: Standardize team database patterns
use_cases.description: Define shared conventions for migrations, indexes, repositories, and query performance.

prompt_templates.title: Create a starter async setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new service.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the database skill to design a basic async SQLModel setup for my Python web app. Include connection management, session cleanup, and testing notes.

prompt_templates.title: Design models and repositories
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate schema and data access planning.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the database skill to design models and repository methods for users, projects, and tasks. Include relationships, indexes, soft deletion, and common queries.

prompt_templates.title: Plan migrations and indexes
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the database skill to plan a migration strategy for a PostgreSQL application. Cover constraints, rollback concerns, indexes, and deployment checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit production performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the database skill to audit my database layer for production readiness. Focus on pooling, slow queries, statistics, backups, encryption, and least privilege.

output_examples.input: I need a database layer for a task application.
output_examples.output: A structured plan covering models, relationships, session lifecycle, repository methods, indexes, migrations, and test fixtures.

output_examples.input: Review my database setup before launch.
output_examples.output: A production checklist covering pooling, SSL, backups, monitoring, slow query thresholds, access controls, and recovery planning.

output_examples.input: Help me improve slow database queries.
output_examples.output: A performance review plan covering query timing, table statistics, index candidates, pagination, and database-specific inspection steps.

best_practices: Require secure connection settings in production and keep secrets outside source files.
Use migrations, indexes, and rollback plans for every schema change.
Test repositories with isolated databases before connecting them to production data.
anti_patterns: Do not copy placeholder connection strings into production systems.
Do not bypass migrations with manual schema changes in live environments.
Do not add dynamic filters without checking allowed model fields and query cost.

faq.question: What databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It focuses on PostgreSQL, MySQL, and SQLite patterns through SQLAlchemy and SQLModel examples.

faq.question: Does the skill execute database commands?
faq.answer: No. It contains guidance and examples that an agent or developer can adapt.

faq.question: Can it help with migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes migration structure, table creation, constraints, indexes, and downgrade planning.

faq.question: Is it only for FastAPI projects?
faq.answer: No. The patterns fit many Python services that use SQLAlchemy or SQLModel.

faq.question: Does it include performance guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers slow query timing, table statistics, indexing, pooling, and production monitoring.

faq.question: Should I use the sample connection strings?
faq.answer: No. Replace placeholders and store real credentials in environment variables or a secrets manager.
